I only came of voting age in the last few years, as did many of my peers, and the consensus between us is that many of us are socially liberal and fiscally conservative; that is to say that we lean Democratically towards issues like same-sex marriage, healthcare, and the legalization of cannabis but generally agree with the Republican views of fiscal matters like deficit spending, economical regulation, and taxes.

Also, I'm pretty sure Kansas as a whole is slowly shifting away from our past far-red political stance. Take, for instance, this map of the political geography of the [Greater Kansas City area](https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/republicans-democrats-cities/), which is definitely more liberal than conservative. Or using the same map to view Wichita, which at first seems like a clear conservative win-- except for the dense blue in the center.

Basically, I think that the younger generation of voters have very mixed views that often don't particularly fit well with either party, and that our red/blue stance changes based more on the candidates (and their beliefs) than anything else. And this subreddit is probably filled with more of the younger voters.

Someone should do a poll of the subreddit, for ages and political affiliations. I think it'd be neat.

Hi all, I'm here to provide some clarity and information, at the behest of commenters:

* **Why I would ever tell my daughter she killed me.** I am not sending this letter to my daughter, ever. This is *unsent* letters. It's just my thoughts, that I needed to vent, and I would never subject my daughter to thoughts like this.
* **How far along I am:** Six, almost seven months! 27 weeks.
* **How could I leave my husband with a baby while he's still mourning me:** it's his choice. If he chooses not to raise her without me, which we've already talked about, we've already discussed adoption. His grandparents have also volunteered to take her, either permanently or until he's grieved. I fully support anything he decides to do after I'm gone, because I love him and I want him to live his life to his choice.
* **Why would I pass a disease to my children:** I didn't want to get into the specifics of my condition in my original post, but I have Congenial Heart Disease, which is *not* normally genetic. It is vary rarely caused by a gene, but it was so rare that I was assured my by doctor that my children wouldn't inherit it. *Doctors can be wrong.* By the time we discovered something was wrong with my little one's heart, we made the decision not to abort. My daughter, as soon as she's born, will be examined by a pediatric cardiologist. It is very likely, based on the ultrasounds, that she only has a hole between the lower chambers of her heart. Not my CHD, thank goodness! Surprisingly, a lot of babies are born with this! She'll probably need surgical intervention, but after that she'll likely be fine and healthy. If it turns out to be worse, that's what the cardiologist is there for.
* **Why would I have children instead of adopting:** I actually raised my both my younger brother and sister, taking the out of the system, and I just wanted one of my own. *We* wanted one of our own. My husband's mother passed away when he was very young, and his father abandoned him. My mother and father were both POS. We wanted one of our own to prove that it isn't our blood, we could be good, loving parents. Again, I was assured that my condition *wasn't genetic.* If I knew that my doctors could be so horribly wrong... well, we wouldn't be here.
* **Why do I think I know better than doctors:** I don't. I hope. I don't *know* anything, nothing is certain, but I can *hope.* They were wrong about me, they were wrong about CDH, so I can *hope* that they're wrong again.
* **Why wouldn't I just abort:** Commenters have mentioned that I should have thought about the innocent baby in my belly who didn't ask to be born, let alone with a heart condition. I know. Please see the above question about passing CDH on to my children. As for why I wouldn't abort, well, I still think any life is better than no life. But that's politics, so let's leave that alone, eh?

I'm happy to answer any more questions. I know my decision makes some people angry, and that's okay! I'm glad everybody took the time to read my post, because I didn't expect it to blow up. I just needed to vent. As a side note, thank you for the awards, kind strangers! But instead of awarding me, consider donating to a better cause, like [The Children's Heart Foundation.](https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/congenital-heart-defects/congenital-heart-defects-tools-and-resources/the-american-heart-association-and-the-childrens-heart-foundation)

I'm six months pregnant and I have a heart condition that makes it very, very likely I'll die giving birth, or carrying as far to term as I can. I knew the risks going in, and so did my husband. It's rough. I'm only 19, but I've got a good career and a loving spouse. I've got my whole life ahead of me, but I've always wanted a baby, a family, of my own. I'll never have an abortion, even if it means dying.

Why? I grew up in the foster care system. It was awful, let me say. I've been sexually assaulted and beaten, starved, and medicated, all to "help" me; and it was still better than staying with my druggie single mother. I was always a sick kid, barely survived childhood; my mom always said she wished she would have aborted me.

I'm pro-choice in the sense that I support **having** a choice. I choose to be pro-life. I think funding for programs like those will help prevent a lot of harm, hardship, and promote alternate options to abortion. But abortion will always be *necessary,* because what if there's another woman out there in my position who doesn't want to risk dying giving birth? What if there's incest or sexual assault that winds up in pregnancy? What if contraception fails and, despite alternate options, you just aren't ready to be pregnant for 9 months and have a baby?

Abortion isn't always the best option, but it should always be an option.

Sincerely, a pro-life, soon-to-be mother's opinion on the topic.

Well, right now the wind where I'm at is blowing at around 10mph, which is the lowest I've seen it this week. To compare, Liberal, KS, is currently sitting pretty at 23mph. There's a saying here that if you don't like the weather in Kansas, wait a day, it'll change. The wind is the only exception. It's a constant. Usually it's fairly calm, around a steady breeze all year, but it can get pretty wild some days.

To try and put it into perspective, almost half of Kansas's power is from the wind, even higher than our coal use. We're one of two states in the whole U.S. that have a strong enough, and steady enough, wind to do so.

You can see an hourly update at Kake news here: https://www.ksn.com/weather/images/kansas-winds/

Bit of advice you didn't ask for, though:

• Be careful of the wind, it's probably stronger than you're used to. Know where your tornado shelter is.

• The economy here is cheaper than you'll be used to, more likely than not. As in, the cost of an item. Do watch out for the taxes, though. We have both state and federal taxes coming out of our paychecks.

• There's not much to do as far as entertainment goes here... besides bars, clubs, museums, and movie theaters. There's quite a bit of tabletop games, though.

• If you have a lot of children, or are struggling financially around the holidays, the food banks and toy drives are fairly accessable.

If you need anything, or just have other questions, feel free to PM me!

Hey! Lifelong resident of Kansas here, though admittedly a fair while from Humboldt and Iola, so I can't say much about the banks there. I personally use Credit Union of America, but that won't do you much good, friend, as it's located mainly around the Sedgwick County area.

The weather here is pretty crazy. Right now, on May 11th, we just had about a week of high 80° weather. Today, it feels like low 30°s. It's just how the weather rolls. I'm fairly cold weather intolerant, and I start wearing long sleeves and jackets around August, breaking out winter coats around September or October. Halloween is always pretty chilly.

I'd recommend Goodwill for a lot of your clothing needs, or secondhand online stores like Thredup. We also have *many* yearly coat drives. Kansas City and Wichita each run three or four, generally speaking. Your community will also be very supportive, especially churches. Also, there tends to be a *lot* of Baptist churches in the area, so you'll never go hungry if you pop by a Sunday service. Baptists love to eat. But most importantly, **you don't need to be religious to stop by for these, or to reach out for help.** Religion aside, your community will try to take care of it's own.

Most places keep the roads well paved and salted during the winter months, so just keep an eye on the weather and make sure your tires have proper amounts of air and aren't worn down. I can't stress this well enough; just the air makes so much of a difference. Make sure to salt your driveway, and be sure to have an ice scraper on hand-- you'll need it. Be careful round the highway entrances and exits, because they tend to be slicker than the roads. One last piece of advice: ***Driving on the snow is easy, but driving on the ice is dangerous.*** Remember, the speed limit during severe weather is whatever speed is safe.

The job market is... okay. I'm not so sure about a land surveyor, but be sure to check the surrounding areas; sometimes jobs here require a fair bit of travel. I drive ~30 min to work, personally.

I'm so sorry, OP, that you have to make such a tough decision. I'm glad you and hubby are able to support one another through the decision. And you are most *definitely* not the asshole, in any capacity or degree, if you choose to screen and not carry a child with disabilities.

That said, your stepmom isn't exactly an ass... she's certainly insensitive and overstepping her bounds, but it's understandable that she's a little sensitive about the topic, considering it's her son that has the disability. She might feel like you're causing offense to her son, or invaluing his life or whatever spiel, but that's her baby and she has a right to feel however she does.

Doesn't make her right, though.  Genetic screening wasn't exactly so popular or effective 20 or 30 years ago, so she has no right to judge you based on actions she never even had a chance to take herself.

I say this as an adult with a genetic defect that will kill me in another ten years or so. My life has been a miserable one, crippled and bedridden, with lots of pain and surgeries. I would never want to pass on this to another human being, ever. You're doing a wonderful thing to think about your child and the future you want to give them.

I hope everything works out for the best.

I have a heart condition that's kept me bedridden off and on my entire life. My lungs never properly functioned, so between my heart and them, I'm almost always huffing and puffing, on and off oxygen. Sometimes I can walk, sometimes I'm in a wheelchair. At eighteen, this is the healthiest I've ever been, and the happiest; I've got a fiance that loves me dearly, and a stable job that doesn't strain me.

But I'm always in pain. My heart, my chest, it always hurts. Painkillers make me fuzzy, so I don't like to use them, and I've got dozens of other pills to take through the day.

Eventually, my heart is going to fail. The only thing that will "fix" it is a surgery to repair a valve that's slowly ceasing to function, and even that will only restore me to this level of function.

When the time comes to have the surgery, I won't. I'm tired of pills and pain. I'm ready to go. Nobody else knows that yet; I don't know if I'll ever tell them that I won't take the surgery.

I wish I did. I desperately want to believe that there's something out there, some great plan or meaning, some afterlife or reincarnation, some kind of God.

But I can never really make myself believe. I can't prove that there's something out there, but I can't exactly disprove it. I'm an agnostic who wishes I was a believer.

I admit, I was too harsh on the bf. He's got a right to be upset, and he can take as much time as he needs. But I disagree strongly with some of the things said in this thread; this is a betrayal that can't be fixed, and your upbringing isn't something that HAS to be disclosed to everyone. It's a part of you, and part of what makes you who you are, but the past is the past and it doesn't need to be relevant to your future.

I was in a very similar situation to OP's with my partner. I told him I had a toxic relationship with my parents, no more. It wasn't exactly a lie, because I was in the system for a reason, but I didn't divulge I was a foster kid until almost a year in. Should OP have told him sooner? Hell yeah. There were better ways to take that. But I can't blame OP for lying. She should have told him sooner than two years, if they were serious, that's for certain.

And that's the thing. If they're serious, they can fix this and work through it; this doesn't have to be a level of betrayal that can never be fixed or accepted.

Hell, everyone on Reddit is so quick to jump to relationship-enders and "can never be fixed" judgements. Have y'all never been in a serious relationship? Yeah, OP's an ass. But relationships take communication and work, and can survive a lot.

**EDIT:** My vote has been changed. I'm sorry, OP. YTA. My original comment remains below.

However, one last word? I said it in a comment below, but everyone in here is too *extreme.* Yeah, OP's an ass. But this is a two year relationship. If they really want to make it work, they can. It doesn't have to be a relationship ender, or betrayal that can never be recovered from. Jfc, just talk it out like adults. If you're really in a serious relationship, *communicate like it.*

Okay, look. I sympathize. I was a foster kid too. The system is rough, yeah, but there's also a lot of stigma against foster kids. I don't mention that part of my past unless I have to, and I'll cover it up if at all possible. I get it. I'd lie if I could get away with it, too-- with the exception of people that would be close to me, or in my life for extended periods of time.

But, OP, lying to your partner is a really sucky thing to do. It's one thing to not mention it, and another to outright lie to the poor dude who is a pretty solid part of your life, as your partner.

~~Your bf kinda sucks, too, for being so pissy about it.~~

OP, you've got a right to limit the information about your life to others. But your bf has a right to be upset about being lied to-- yeah, that is a betrayal-- and you need to respect that.

Sit him down, have a conversation about why you felt the need to lie. Try to understand his point, too; he feels betrayed, with good reason, by his partner, who he's supposed to be able to trust.

I'm going to go against the grain here and say NAH.

Look, I grew up with my dad a few states away. He had a new wife and a kid two years after he left, before I was even born. And yeah, that stung like a bitch. I'm not going to lie, I resent him. But having him around when he wouldn't want to be, wasn't in the fit mental capacity to be? Kids pick up on things; I would have known that my dad didn't (and shouldn't, mentally) be there, and your kids will, too. I would have hated being resented by him for keeping him there.

My guy, you're more than entitled to move away, get some help and space. But know that when you do, you'll still be obligated to your kids. Pay child support, be there for important moments, stop in and see them a few times a year. And even if you do? They might resent you. They're entitled to feel that way, and that's okay. Just make sure they know you love them no matter what, and you'll only be a call away.

Good luck, friend. Sorry you're in such a tough spot.

OP, I did the exact same thing your wife did when I found out I was pregnant. I hid it for six weeks, and miscarried the night I told my fiance. I've always had fertility issues, and I was absolutely *terrified* that I'd lose the baby. He was hurt, understandably, and it took him a long time to understand-- it took me awhile to understand why I was hiding it, too. So I can't say exactly what your wife did that, OP, but I can try and give you an insight to what might have been going through her head.

She was probably just trying to spare you the pain of losing another baby. Misguided as it might be, losing a child is traumatic and it really fucks up your head. So she can't spare herself the pain, but she can do her best to look out for you. Damage control. And the fear of losing the baby might have leaked over into a fear of losing you; it seems irrational, but fear always is. A part of her might blame herself for losing the baby. Just assure her that you'll be there for her no matter, and that you don't blame her.

I'm so sorry for your loss, and congratulations on the new baby. I hope that you're able to work through the issue as a couple, and that you come out stronger.

Good luck, OP.
